accuracy.reason: Live MySQL 8.4 primary documentation verifies InnoDB scope, mode-dependent conversion, autocommit, Repeatable Read with own-change exception, index representation, asynchronous loss and backup-plus-log recovery. No unconditional scaling or freshness promise.

evidence.quote: Later plain SELECTs reuse it, while still seeing that transaction's own changes.

mechanisms.reason: Every card objective is taught: separate server/engine roles, explicit rules and transaction boundaries, protected locking-read changes and deadlock retry, secondary-to-clustered lookup, receipt versus apply, and distinct recovery mechanisms. Diagram arrows and captions preserve these meanings.

evidence.quote: Check and change the protected value before committing; an earlier unprotected check does not reserve it.

coherence.reason: Engine capabilities are established before constraints and ACID. Concurrency then motivates index/lock cost, with replication and historical recovery feeding the final requirement-led choice. The defined SQL/transaction prerequisites suffice.

evidence.quote: These costs follow from the mechanisms covered in this deck.

decisions.reason: Workload and failure targets govern engine/schema, bounded transactions/connections, measured indexes and replica routing; historical recovery and source write limits prevent treating product selection as sufficient.

evidence.quote: Clarify read/write traffic, stale-read tolerance, acknowledged-write loss, write latency and downtime.

clarity.reason: Unfamiliar terms are defined and price/type examples selectively clarify behavior. ACID and isolation cards are dense, but their necessary distinctions remain readable and none of the required mechanisms depends on unexplained jargon.

evidence.quote: Automatically commits each successful statement as its own transaction when no explicit transaction is open.

outcomes.reason: All six criteria supported: actual learner traces relational server requests and shared clients, distinguishes unresolved schema/workload/recovery choices, scopes guarantees to InnoDB and bounds row-lock contention.

All eight criteria supported: learner specifies types/keys/null/check/reference rules and mode/version checks, explicit grouped transaction versus autocommit, declared invariants, bounded persistence and external-action limits.

All eight criteria supported: learner correctly bounds first-plain-read snapshot and own changes, uses a protected current locking read/check/change transaction, handles no allocation and full-transaction deadlock retry, and explains clustered/secondary key size, plan measurement, scan alternatives and index costs. Its general write-maintenance wording is understood as applicable index work, not a guarantee every write changes every index.

All eight criteria supported: actual learner distinguishes source/binlog receipt/application lag and async loss, policy-based fresh reads/promotion, local crash recovery versus failover/history, accidental deletion propagation, compatible base backup plus continuous logs and measured restore tests.

All four criteria supported: conditional InnoDB fit retains schema and concurrency choices, workload/index costs, suitable replica reads and finite source writes, bounded connections/transactions and explicit loss/freshness/latency/downtime requirements with tested recovery.

sourceChecks.claim: MySQL what-is-mysql page verifies client/server SQL with relational tables and relationships; does not replace workload-specific design.
InnoDB introduction verifies default engine, transactional commit/rollback/crash recovery and row-level locking; guarantees are scoped to the engine.
SQL-mode documentation explicitly verifies abc-to-INT error in strict mode versus 0 plus warning otherwise; official CHECK documentation verifies FALSE rejection and enforcement configuration.
COMMIT documentation verifies default autocommit and explicit grouping/rollback; InnoDB persistence parameter documentation verifies configurable flush behavior and recent-commit loss exposure.

InnoDB isolation and consistent-read documentation verify first consistent-read snapshot plus own changes; locking-read and deadlock followups verify current protected changes and aborted-transaction retry.
InnoDB index-types page verifies clustered row storage, secondary primary-key payload and larger entries for long primary keys; diagram correctly allows covered reads to avoid the extra lookup.
MySQL replication documentation verifies binary-log events and asynchronous versus receipt acknowledgement; GTID application-wait documentation verifies receipt is not proof of readable application.
MySQL point-in-time recovery and binary-log recovery followup verify a full base backup and subsequent logs replayed to the intended point, with required retained history.
InnoDB introduction and checked locking/index/replication/recovery documentation support requirement-led benefits and costs; no automatic write scaling or recovery target is asserted.
